title: Theft of animals and the night thief

plan.english: If anyone steals a cow, he shall give ten cows. If anyone steals a horse, he shall lead five swift horses. If anyone steals a sheep, he shall give two sheep. If anyone drives a dog out of the enclosure, let him lead a goose. If he says: "I did not steal", he shall take the oath. If he lies in the oath, let him give twice. If anyone seizes the one stealing, in the cow-stall at night, let him kill him. But if the sun has become bright, let him not kill him; let him lead him to the king.

title: The price of a hand, an eye and a nose

plan.english: If anyone breaks a man's hand, the price of a hand is three cattle. If anyone wounds an eye, the price of an eye is four geese. If anyone cuts off a nose, the price of a nose is two sheep. If a son-in-law strikes his own father-in-law, let him give wool. If a brother-in-law wounds his own brother-in-law, let him give a garment. Whoever kills a man, let him give four bound ones, and he shall take the oath.

If a man leads a woman to his own village, he shall give the bride price to her father. The bride price of a free woman is ten cattle. If the father does not take it, let her not be led away. Whoever leads a woman and does not give the bride price, let him give twice. If the father dies, let the son take it. If a woman flees from her husband, let her father give back the bride price. Let the daughter-in-law not leave the village of her father-in-law.

If anyone burns a man's enclosure, he shall build another enclosure. Whoever sets fire, and the cow-stall burns, let him give the price of the cow-stall. If the wind drives the fire in, let no one give the price. Whoever sees the fire, let him cry out. Let the daughter-in-law bring water.

If a wolf devours a sheep, let the shepherd not give its price. If the shepherd lets it go and a wolf devours it, he shall give its price. If a sheep goes astray, let him seek it; if he finds it, let him lead it back. If he says: "The wolf devoured it", he shall take the oath by Sky. The dog of the shepherd is dear. Whoever kills it, let him give two geese.

A guest is dear. Whoever kills a guest, let his name vanish. Whoever guards a guest, may he have good fame. If two guests come, let the man seat them. Let the woman give them water and clothe them. A pledge is strong; whoever breaks the pledge, let him give twice.

If anyone yokes a man's two horses and drives them and a horse dies, he shall give a horse. If a son-in-law drives the wagon of his father-in-law and breaks it, let him give a wagon. The wage for a wagon is two geese. The wage for a yoke is a goose.

If anyone has no son, let his brother take the field. If anyone dies, let the sons take the horses. Let the mother take the garments and the wool. Let the two brothers not split it. If a husband dies, let the husband's brother lead the woman, and let him give the bride price to her father.
If a bound one flees and a man seizes him, let him lead him back. Whoever frees a bound one, let him give two bound ones and he shall take the oath. The price of a bound one is ten cattle.

Whoever has seen a man stealing, let him say the word to the king. Whoever has seen it and does not speak, let him give a goose. The word of two men is strong. If anyone lies in the oath, let him give ten geese.
The price of a horse is ten cattle. The price of a dog is a goose. The wage of a shepherd is a sheep. The bride price of a free woman is ten cattle. Whoever gives the price, let him take the horse.

I am the king of good fame. Hear my word, men! Let no one lead a man's wife away. Let no one break the wall of the village. Let no one break the pledge. Whoever does not hear the king's word, let him not dwell in the village.
If a shepherd guards a man's sheep, the man shall give him the wage. If he does not give the wage, let him give it twice. Let the shepherd stand up and speak. Let both give a pledge.
Whoever leads water into a man's field, let him give a goose. If someone's cattle drink the water of another, he shall give its price. Whoever sees a wild beast, let him kill it.

title: Oath by Father Sky and Mother Earth

plan.english: Father Sky and Mother Earth, hear me! I took the oath. I did not steal this man's cow. I did not lead away his daughter-in-law. I did not break the pledge. I did not strike my father-in-law. If I deceive you, strike me, Sky! Swallow me, Earth! May my name vanish, and may my sons not live.

title: The Sun, the eye of Sky

plan.english: The Sun is the eye of Sky. Sun, you who look at the earth, who have seen the hands of men, look at my hands! My two strong hands did not seize the sheep of my brother-in-law. They did not break the pledge. If I deceive, may the sun not become bright for me; may night seize me.

title: The pledge of father-in-law and son-in-law

plan.english: Father-in-law, you and I took the pledge. I shall give you the bride price, and you shall give me the woman. I shall not steal your horses; you shall not drive off my cattle. If I break the pledge, strike me, Sky! If you break it, may the Earth swallow you. May Sky and Earth see us two, and may the gods hear us.

Whoever breaks this oath, may Sky strike him. May the Earth not carry him, and may the Sun not look at him. May fire burn his enclosure and his cow-stall. May a big wolf devour his sheep and his dog. May his horses vanish, and may his sons not live. May his daughter-in-law leave his house, and may his brothers-in-law not hear his name. But whoever keeps the oath, may he have imperishable fame.

I took the oath by the Earth in the village. I did not flee from my husband. I milked the sheep and protected the fire. I did not give the wool to a stranger. I did not strike my husband's brother. If I deceive, may the Earth not carry me, and may my husband lead another woman.

I did not eat the sheep. A big wolf came in the night. I saw the wolf and heard the sheep crying out. I threw my spear; the wolf fled. I did not take the wool of my father-in-law. I took the oath by the gods. If I deceive, may wolves devour me, and may my dog not follow me.

Hear us, Perkunos! We brothers-in-law took the oath. We shall stand together in war. We shall not flee from the war, and we shall not leave a brother. Whoever flees, may your spear strike him. Whoever stands up, may he have imperishable fame.

title: The pledge of host and guest

plan.english: Guest, you and I took the pledge. I shall give you water; I shall seat you at my fire. You shall not steal from my enclosure, and you shall not lead my wife away. My son is your son, and your son is my son. Whoever breaks the pledge, may Sky strike him.

title: Oath by fire, water and spear

plan.english: I took the oath by fire, by water and by the spear. I did not break the pledge. If I deceive, burn me, Fire! Swallow me, Water! Wound me, Spear!

I am the king, the shepherd of men. Hear me, men and gods! I shall guard the village. I shall set the word straight. I shall not take the field of a man. I shall not lead the men into war. If I deceive you, may my name vanish, and may the gods not hear me.
I stand in this field. This is the field of my father-in-law. His father ploughed it. My father-in-law gave it to me with the bride price. Sun, see my words! If I deceive, may fire burn it.

My husband's brother and I took the oath. We shall not split the field; we shall drive the cattle together. The word of my husband's brother is my word. If I deceive my husband's brother, strike me, Sky! If my husband's brother deceives me, strike him!

I saw with these two eyes, yesterday at night, a man leading a cow out of the cow-stall. I know the man. I say the word to the king. I did not lie to the king. If I lie, may these two eyes not see the sun.

It dawned. The brother-in-law and the husband's brother came to the father. They had a great field. The brother-in-law said: "The father-in-law gave it to me." The husband's brother said: "He gave it to me." The father heard the words of both, and said: "Who saw the father-in-law giving it?" No one spoke. The father-in-law had died. Then the father said: "Let both take the oath. Whoever takes it, let him take the field." The brother-in-law took the oath by the gods. The husband's brother became afraid and did not take it. The two went home, and peace was between the brothers-in-law.

At dawn the father-in-law came to the king and said: "My son-in-law stole my yoke in the night." The king said: "Son-in-law, take the oath." The son-in-law said: "I did not steal the yoke." He took the oath by the Sun. Then the barefoot shepherd stood up and said: "In the night I heard the dogs crying out. I came, and I saw the son-in-law carrying the yoke." The son-in-law became afraid. The king said: "Let him give ten cattle to his own father-in-law." The son-in-law gave them, and peace was theirs.

title: The goose that knows her nest

plan.english: A goose stood in the village. The brother-in-law said: "This is my goose." The husband's brother said: "This is my goose." Then the mother said: "Let the goose go." The goose went to the nest of the husband's brother and stood there. The brother-in-law did not speak. The husband's brother led the goose away. The mother said: "The goose knows its own nest."

The shepherd said to his father-in-law: "I guarded your sheep and I milked them. You did not give me the wage." The father-in-law said: "A big wolf devoured two sheep in the night. You let them go." The shepherd said: "I saw the wolf. I threw my spear and it fled." Then they went and saw the track of the wolf. The father-in-law said: "The track of the wolf lies in the field. You guarded them. I shall give you the wage twice."

The husband's brother came to the father and said: "This brother-in-law killed my brother." The brother-in-law said: "The brother of that man came at me with a spear. I struck him in the heart and he died." The husband's brother said: "Let that one die!" The father said: "Do not kill the brother-in-law. Let him give four bound ones and ten cattle." The husband's brother led away the bound ones and the cattle, and the brother-in-law lived.

title: The horse that died in the yoke

plan.english: The father-in-law said to his son-in-law: "I gave you my two horses. You yoked them and drove them to another village. One horse died." The son-in-law said: "On the way the horse slipped, and it died. Did I strike it? I did not strike it." The father-in-law said: "Take the oath." The son-in-law took the oath by the Sun. The father-in-law went along the way and saw the track of the horse. He said: "The oath is strong. May there be peace for us."

The father-in-law came to the king with his own son-in-law and said: "This man led the woman from my village and did not give the bride price." The son-in-law said: "I gave ten sheep. The mother of the woman saw them." Then the mother stood up and said: "I saw them in the enclosure of my husband." The king said: "The word of the mother is strong." The father-in-law did not speak. Then the king said: "Let her dwell in the village of her husband."

It rained, and the wind was great. Fire burned the cow-stall of the brother-in-law. He said to the husband's brother: "You set fire." That one said: "I set fire, but the wind drove it into your enclosure." Then the daughter-in-law said: "I saw the wind driving the fire." The husband's brother took the oath by Fire and by Water. The brother-in-law became afraid and did not speak. Peace was theirs.

title: The daughter-in-law who changed her word

plan.english: The daughter-in-law stood up before the king and said: "Yesterday I saw the husband's brother in the cow-stall." Then she came again and said: "I saw the husband's brother in the field." The king said: "Yesterday you saw him in the cow-stall. Now you see him in the field. You lie to me. Take the oath." She trembled and did not take the oath. The king said: "Let her give ten geese to the husband's brother." She gave them.

The daughter-in-law said to the husband's brother: "The guest took my garment." The husband's brother said to the guest: "Say the word." The guest said: "I did not take the garment. I drank water at your fire and lay down. In the night I did not stand up." Then the daughter-in-law went into the enclosure and found the garment there. She said: "You are dear, guest. I put the garment in the enclosure and I do not remember." The husband's brother seated the guest at his fire.

The father-in-law of the eastern village and the husband's brother of the other village came to the father. The first said: "Our fathers led the water into the field." The second said: "The water comes from our village. Our sheep are thirsty, and you lead it away." The first took the oath by the Earth. The famous father said: "Let the water go to the two villages. Let the first lead it at dawn. Let the second lead it in the night." The two gave a pledge of peace.

title: The two wagons on the way

plan.english: Two sons-in-law drove two wagons on the way. The two wagons came together, and a wheel broke. This one said: "That one struck me." That one said: "This one struck me." Then the shepherd stood up and said: "I saw the two wagons. The swift horses of this son-in-law ran and struck the wheel of that one." Then this one said: "I shall give the price of the wheel. May there be peace between us."

title: The father's word about the field

plan.english: A man died. His sons came to the brother of their father. They took the cattle and they sought the field. Then the daughter-in-law stood up and said: "My father-in-law said: Whoever ploughs the field, let him take it." The brother said: "Who ploughed the field?" The second son said: "I ploughed the field with my father." The brother said: "The word of the father is strong. Let the second son take it."
